A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV-1 infection induces miRNAs expression that are upregulated in HIV-1 exposed individuals.

HIV-1 infection is able to modify miRNAs expression in both HIV+ and HESN subjects, and some of those miRNAs are specifically increased in the latter, suggesting that their modulation may play a role in natural resistance to this pathogen.
miRNAs could represent a novel biomarker for HIV-1 exposure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the identification of miRNAs specifically upregulated in HESN could be a promising approach for the development of new therapeutic strategies to control HIV-1 infection.
miRNA expression can be modified in HIV-1 exposure, even when there is not productive infection.
HIV exposure can alter miRNAs expression in the absence of HIV replication.
